To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(i) methane oxidation and the methane-oxidizing community are spatially distributed in a riparian forest, (ii) the spatial pattern of methane-oxidizer community structure is reflected in the environmental gradient, (iii) with smaller plot size, local factors become more important and (iv) environmental gradients can generally be used to explain spatial patterns of microorganisms but do not contribute to a mechanism of microbial diversity.
(i) methane oxidation and the abundance of MOB were positively correlated and (ii) the spatial distribution of the MOB was driven by the flooding gradient.

(i) the spatial variability of MOB is reflected in the underlying hydrological gradient; (ii) type I MOB and type II MOBs display overlapping and contrasting spatial patterns, suggesting different ecological life strategies; (iii) smaller plot size leads to a higher spatial variability and a less explanatory role of the environmental gradient.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the question of how the spatial patterns of microbial communities can be explained by environmental gradients and whether this is scale-dependent.
the question of how the environment influences microbial communities, but it does not provide an answer to this question.
the question of whether environmental gradients explain spatial patterns of MOB.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
environmental gradients are important for the distribution of microbial communities but that they are not sufficient to fully explain the variability in spatial patterns.
microbial spatial patterns can be explained by large-scale environmental factors but not by small-scale factors, and that this is dependent on plot size.
the spatial distribution of microbial communities depends on the scale of investigation.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
MOB are not evenly distributed across the floodplain and that the spatial patterns of MOB are reflected by the environmental gradient.

the spatial variability of methane oxidation is mainly determined by the spatial variability of flooding and the spatial variability of MOB communities is mainly determined by their spatial variability of methane availability and the presence or absence of flooding.
the MOB communities in our wetland were spatially structured and that this structure was driven by the hydrological gradient.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the scale at which environmental variables are measured is crucial in determining microbial spatial patterns.
the scale of sampling is crucial for understanding spatial patterns of microorganisms and their environment.
the spatial variability of MOB is driven by the environmental gradient and that smaller scales can be important for the understanding of the spatial variability of microorganisms.
